svg.title: Three clocks and two failure paths in a proposed hold-release schedule
svg.desc: The ten-minute business deadline, proposed one-minute Scheduler tick, and two-hour lab stop are different clocks. The schedule is a design exercise pending account and cost review. Scheduler delivery failure goes to a delivery dead-letter queue; an accepted asynchronous Lambda request can fail during code execution and needs a separate on-failure destination. A tick examines at most fifteen visible index entries, so later passes and customer-state checks remain necessary.
svg.text: Three clocks. Two failure routes.
Design-only schedule; enable after account and cost review.
Keep the clocks separate
Business deadline · minute 10
The hold becomes ineligible; release may happen later.
Proposed Scheduler tick · every minute
One pass sees at most 15 visible index entries.
A quiet pass does not prove every due hold was found.
Lab stop · at most two hours
The handler stops new work; resources stay deployed.
Follow the request and its failure route
1 Scheduler attempts delivery
A successful delivery is not successful code.
Route A · delivery fails → Scheduler DLQ
The target request was not accepted.
Route B · Lambda accepts and runs the tick
Read the base hold; release it conditionally.
If code fails → Lambda on-failure destination
Earlier pages may have committed; reconcile first.
Even after success, check backlog and actual customer seat state.
